Unguarded ByteBuffer allocator exception in GcsFooterOptimizer.readVectored stranded all subsequent range CompletableFutures because SmartReadChannel.readVectored has no try/catch, plus potential over-copy on oversized buffers.
InMemoryStorage dynamic Proxy routed Object.equals/hashCode/toString to fail-loud UnsupportedOperationException handler.
HermeticGcsFileSystem created non-daemon ExecutorService threads that would hang JUnit and JMH fork JVMs when streams were not explicitly closed.
getGcsItemInfo returned GcsItemInfo.createNotFound for missing objects instead of throwing FileNotFoundException like production GcsClientImpl.
SmallObjectCacheBenchmark.coldRead instantiated a fresh HermeticGcsFileSystem (and thread pool) per invocation instead of calling cacheManager.invalidateSmallObject(itemId).
Empty OperationListener callbacks allowed C2 JIT scalar replacement of MetricKey and singletonMap; consuming into a volatile sink corrected recordMetric from 3.0 ns/op to 11.7 ns/op.

The project style guide mandates always using try-with-resources for AutoCloseable types (like GcsWriteChannel), even when explicitly testing the close() method. Using try-with-resources guarantees cleanup if the constructor or assertions fail prematurely.

The project style guide mandates always using try-with-resources for AutoCloseable types (like GcsBidiWriteChannel), even when explicitly testing the close() method. Using try-with-resources guarantees cleanup if the constructor or assertions fail prematurely.

The explicit EOF short-circuit block added to `readFully` duplicates channel opening/reading logic and drops `adoptResolvedItemInfo`. Crucially, it assumes `byteChannel.read(...)` returns exactly `available` bytes by ignoring its return value. If a short read occurs, the `EOFException` will incorrectly report `length - available` bytes left instead of the actual missing amount. This complexity is unnecessary. If bounding the request size is desired, calculate a capped `bytesToRead` and pass it to the existing `read(...)` call.

The evidence chain is broken because the unit gate failed with an ERROR status (build failures, NoClassDefFoundError, and compiler exceptions in the logs). A PR cannot be approved if the tests do not pass.
The dst.position(...) call in readUpTo is redundant. The ReadableByteChannel.read(dst) contract guarantees that the buffer's position is automatically advanced by the number of bytes read.

The caching of `positionalReadOptions` on the stream instance is ineffective for short-lived streams (which is the typical use case for single-shot `readTail` and `readFully`). As a result, `GcsReadOptions.toBuilder().build()` is invoked on every single stream creation + read, causing a 41% allocation rate regression in `FooterPrefetchBenchmark.readTail`. The cache should ideally live at a higher scope (e.g., in `GcsClientOptions`) or be avoided if it requires heavy rebuilding.

The `openReadChannel` lambda now captures `readOptions` from the enclosing method arguments, whereas previously it fetched it from the file system internally. This increased the capture size and likely defeated C2's escape analysis for the lambda, leading to a massive 53% allocation regression (+1612 bytes/op) and latency regression in `GcsReadChannelOpenBenchmark.openAndReadOneByte_withFileInfo`.

The loop prematurely terminates when `read == 0`. This contradicts the PR hypothesis 'avoiding any premature termination on 0-byte yields'. If the channel momentarily yields 0 bytes without reaching EOF, this will incorrectly throw an EOFException in `readFully`.
The loop allocates a new `ByteBuffer` on each iteration using `ByteBuffer.wrap()`, contradicting the hypothesis' claim of using 'automatic ByteBuffer position advancement'.

Catching `Throwable` swallows fatal JVM errors like `OutOfMemoryError` or `ThreadDeath`. While completing the future exceptionally is safe, masking such errors can leave the system in an unstable state.
Test relies on Mockito's default behavior of returning `Optional.empty()` for unstubbed methods returning `Optional`. This can be fragile across Mockito versions.

The cache population method `addMatchingZeroArgMethods` calls `method.setAccessible(true)` without catching `RuntimeException`. On Java 9+, `setAccessible(true)` can throw `InaccessibleObjectException` for public methods of classes in closed modules. In the original code, this was safely caught by `invokeLongGetter`'s `try...catch (ReflectiveOperationException | RuntimeException e)`, allowing graceful fallback to the next getter or returning `-1L`. In this new code, an inaccessible getter will crash `ClassValue.computeValue` and fail the entire `extract()` method. You must catch and ignore `RuntimeException` around `setAccessible` here, just like you did in `ChannelAccessors.forClass`.
